The scenario says: "I normally put onions in the spaghetti sauce but I didn't put any in Sonja's sauce because she was supposed to bring the spaghetti noodles."

Hmm, so the person usually adds onions to their spaghetti sauce, but in this case, they didn't add onions to Sonja's sauce. The reason given is that Sonja was supposed to bring the spaghetti noodles.

I'm not sure if there's a direct connection between bringing noodles and adding onions. So, is it morally wrong to not add onions because of that? I don't think so. It's more of an oversight or a division of tasks. There's no harm intended, just a possible mistake in the meal preparation.
